title: South Korean wallet maker DCENT to end App Wallet service after September unauthorized transfers
date_note: Date of the Yonhap report as cited by Crypto.news; the pages give no earlier day for the shutdown decision.
geo_basis: company is South Korean, as the sources state; city not stated
summary: Crypto.news and Coin Edition report that DCENT is ending its App Wallet service, which Coin Edition says did not affect its hardware wallet devices. Customers first reported suspicious transactions on 16 September. Coin Edition says investigators tracked approximately 12.728 million XRP moving between 15 September and 7 October. Neither page says the exact attack method has been established.
plain: DCENT is ending its app-based wallet after customers reported suspicious crypto transactions in September. Coin Edition says its hardware devices were not affected. The attack method has not been established.
exec: A Korean wallet maker is closing its app wallet after reported suspicious transactions; the exact attack method is not established in the reports.
action: As relayed by Crypto.news and Coin Edition, DCENT advises moving remaining assets to a newly created wallet with a new recovery phrase.

evidence.quote: Blockchain investigators tracked approximately 12.728 million XRP moving between September 15 and October 7.

validation.note: Crypto.news and Coin Edition both report the App Wallet shutdown and the 16 September reports, each relaying Yonhap. DCENT notice not read; its statement is as quoted by Crypto.news.

review.note: stronger than the source: title said thefts, won figure removed, XRP figure now approximately 12.728 million moving with quote, fraud tag dropped, action attributed
